sentences.text:
Pawan vs Shantilal Khandelwal on 6 April, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Ind:9063
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Binod Kumar Dwivedi

On The 6 th Of April, 2026
 Misc. Appeal No. 4430 of 2025
 Pawan
 Versus
 Shantilal Khandelwal And Others
 Appearance:
 Ms. Ayushi Thakur - Advocate for the appellant.

Ms. Priti Keshwani - Advocate for respondent No.2.
 Order
Liability is not in dispute in the present appeal, therefore, service of notice on respondent No.1 is dispensed with.

2. This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 against the impugned award dated 08/04/2025 passed by 29th Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (M.P.) in MACC No.3465/2021, whereby an amount of Rs.9,32,558/- has been awarded from the date of filing of claim petition to the appellant / claimant with interest @ 6%
per annum.
3.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in the accident appellant has sustained fracture of right Tibia Fibula Bone.
He has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 30%.

Disability Certificate is Ex.-P/8, which has been proved by Dr. Ashish Malhotra (AW-2), however, the learned Claims Tribunal has failed to appreciate the evidence in this regard NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:9063 2 MA-4430-2025 and has awarded compensation amount considering the disability only at 10%, whereas looking to the nature of injury it should be at least 15% to the whole proportion of the body.
3.1 Learned counsel further submits that the amount awarded in the head of conveyance is on lower side, therefore, prays for enhancing the same adequately.
On these grounds, learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award amount.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that evidence led before the learned Claims Tribunal has been rightly appreciated.
The amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.

1
All the factors have been considered by the learned Claims Tribunal while awarding the compensation amount and no fault can be found with in the impugned award.
He further submits that the amount awarded in the head of special diet is on higher side, which require interference by this Court.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the appeal being devoid of any substance as aforesaid.

5. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.

From perusal of the evidence with regard to disability suffered by the appellant, it is apparent that appellant has sustained fracture of right Tibia Fibula Bone and Dr. Ashish Malhotra (AW-2) has proved the disability to the extent of 30%.

Disability Certificate (Ex.-P/8) is also on record,
therefore, this Court is of the view that disability should be assessed at least NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:9063 3 MA-4430-2025 15% to the whole proportion of the body, therefore,

the same is taken at 15%.
7.

Learned Claims Tribunal has awarded only Rs.3,000/- in the head of conveyance, which appears on lower side, therefore, the same is enhanced from Rs.3,000/- to Rs.5,000/-, which will be the just and proper compensation in this head.
8. The amount awarded in the head of special diet Rs.9,000/- is on higher side, therefore, the same is reduced from Rs.9,000/- to Rs.5,000/-.
The amount awarded in the other heads has not been disputed by the either party, which appears just and proper, hence no interference is required.

9. Accordingly, the just and proper compensation amount comes as under:
15% PD comes to Rs.8,63,250/-
Permanent Disability: [Rs.39,635/- pm + 10% FP x 12 Months x Multiplier of 11]
Medical Expenses: Rs.1,99,155/-
 Conveyance: Rs.5,000/-
 Special Diet: Rs.5,000/-
 Attendant: Rs.2,000/-
 Pain and Suffering: Rs.25,000/-
 Loss of Income: Rs.1,18,905/- (for 3 Months)
 Total Amount: Rs.12,18,310/-
 MACT Awarded: Rs.9,32,558/-
 Enhanced Amount: Rs.2,85,752/-
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.12,18,310/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.9,32,558/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.2,85,752/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.

2 10.
Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellant / claimant is allowed to the extent as indicated hereinabove.

Other terms and conditions of the impugned award including rate of interest @ 6%
shall remain intact.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Tej Pawan vs Shantilal Khandelwal on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80585750/
